title: Kernel hot-swap race causing microbatch starvation under capacity pressure
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a capacity surge on 2026-02-14 we observed repeated p95/p99 latency spikes on hosted inference routes. Investigation identified a race in the kernel hot-swap state machine that could leave a subset of workers briefly unable to accept microbatches (100-400ms). This manifested as feed-forward starvation: the scheduler would continue to queue requests but microbatch assembly stalled because hot-swap left worker local queues in a transient invalid state. The event correlated with simultaneous kernel swaps (quant <-> fused-attn) triggered by an autoscale burst and concurrent KV-cache warmups. The symptom set: p95 spikes, increased request timeouts, increased requeues to fallback paths, and elevated service errors on a small subset of customers. This ticket captures follow-ups, mitigations, and rollout plan to prevent recurrence.
reproduction_steps: 1) Start a synthetic burst using ab-initio-bench with 200 concurrent clients targeting a 512-token LLM route
2) Ensure autoscaler is set to conservative scale-up thresholds (simulate delayed provisioning)
3) Force mixed-quant kernel candidate probing by toggling quant-profile at runtime via test harness
4) Observe worker logs for hot-swap state transitions and microbatch queue drain rate
5) Reproduce p95 spikes locally in staging using the same sequence of swaps and KV-cache invalidations

root_cause_summary: A concurrency bug in the kernel hot-swap state machine allowed a transient invalid state where worker acceptor threads paused microbatch intake while the scheduler continued to mark capacity available. This was most likely when multiple kernel candidates were probed in quick succession while KV cache warmup was concurrently reassigning memory buffers. The mismatch between the worker life-cycle (hot-swap) and the scheduler's admission control caused microbatch starvation until state reconciler completed. Tightly-coupled autoscale bursts amplified the window and increased customer-visible tail latency.
action_items: A1: Add assertable invariants to hot-swap state machine and unit tests for transition combos (owner: Diego Morales, estimate: 3)
A2: Integrate worker-level admission-control: workers must signal 'ready_for_microbatch' before scheduler assigns new microbatches (owner: Linh Tran, estimate: 5)
A3: Add metrics and alerting: hot_swap_invalid_state_count, microbatch_drain_rate_by_worker, and a derived alarm when drain_rate==0 for >200ms (owner: Priya Shah, estimate: 2)
A4: Implement a short serialization window for hot-swap operations behind feature flag and rollout to 10% of capacity (owner: Diego Morales, estimate: 2)
A5: Add synthetic e2e test to CI that simulates autoscale+kernel-probing bursts and validates no starvation (owner: QA team - Marcus Lee, estimate: 3)
A6: Update runtime playbook and SRE runbook with remediation steps: toggle serialize-hot-swap, route fallback, and decrease probe aggressiveness (owner: SRE - Jamie Nguyen, estimate: 1)
A7: Post-deploy: 2-week telemetry watch with daily rollout-to-100% decision checkpoint (owner: Diego Morales, estimate: 1)
A8: Audit related scheduler heuristics to ensure they respect worker readiness signals (owner: Scheduler team - Erin O'Connor, estimate: 4)
mitigations_deployed: Short-term: feature-flagged serialize-hot-swap=true deployed to all clusters on 2026-02-14 (reduced incidence but not root-fixed)
Medium-term: PR #4281 opened to gate scheduler assignment on worker readiness; currently in review
Operational: temporary expand fallback routing and increased timeouts for affected customers during containment window
reviews: PM review (Omar Ruiz): confirm customer communication and SLAs are handled; suggested adding customer_impact field and prioritizing high-throughput customers for canary
Design review (Nina Park): no UX changes required, but console should surface worker readiness as a new telemetry panel
Security review: not required for this fix (no data-plane changes), security sign-off by Priya Sharma
followup_notes: We observed secondary signals from KV cache warmup increasing memory churn; pairing with Mike R.'s team to verify buffer reuse semantics
Consider a longer-term architecture item: decouple kernel candidate probing from immediate worker hot-swap by staging new kernels in a 'pending' state
Ops suggested a small change to autoscaler hysteresis to avoid simultaneous specimen scale-ups during high variance traffic patterns
closure_criteria: Invariant tests and unit coverage for all hot-swap transitions merged to main
Worker readiness signals implemented and scheduler respects them in canary rollout
No recurrence of starvation spikes in 14 days post 100% rollout across regions
Playbook updated and SRE runbook distribution confirmed
